text:
We'll use $n$ as short for $\Value{
um{n}}{M}$, a standard
!!{element} of~$\Struct{M}$.  Already $\Th{Q}$ proves that, for any~$n
\in \Nat$, $\lforall[x][(x < 
um{n}' \lif (\eq[x][
um{0}] \lor
  \eq[x][
um{1}] \lor \dots \lor \eq[x][
um{n}]))]$. There are no
!!{element}s that are $
sless 
szero$. So if $n$ is standard and $x$
is non-standard, we cannot have $x 
sless n$. By definition, a
non-standard element is one that isn't $\Value{
um{n}}{M}$ for any~$n
\in \Nat$, so $x 
eq n$ as well. Since $
sless$ is a linear order,
we must have $n 
sless x$.
